summary: VIDYA: an adaptive moving average that speeds up in strong moves and slows in quiet ones, colored by trend regime.
overview: The Variable Index Dynamic Average (VIDYA) is a moving average whose speed changes bar by bar. It moves faster when momentum is strong and almost stops when the market is quiet.
With Trend Regime Coloring on, it is green while sloping up, red while sloping down and gray when flat. The adaptive gradient fades the color as momentum dies.
how: VIDYA starts from an EMA smoothing share of 2 / (N + 1), with N = 12 by default, and multiplies it by a scaler each bar. In Momentum mode the scaler is the absolute Chande Momentum Oscillator (9 bars) divided by 100. In Volatility mode it is a short standard deviation divided by a reference standard deviation (30 bars).
The line counts as flat when its one-bar change is below 0.05 of ATR(14).
use: Use the flat color to spot ranges where the average stops moving.
Some traders watch the regime color change as a sign of a new trend.
Use it as a trend line that stays still in noise.
Compare Momentum and Volatility modes to see which suits the symbol.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It can stay flat for long periods in quiet markets.
